t.7.75.1: When Rāma had spoken thus, and the great-souled Bharata as well, Lakṣmaṇa too spoke auspicious words to the delight of the Raghus.
t.7.75.2: The Aśvamedha, the great sacrifice, is the purifier of all sins; let that invincible purifier, the foremost of sacrifices, be pleasing to you.
t.7.75.3: For an ancient tale is heard concerning the most great-souled Vāsava: Śakra, enveloped by the sin of slaying a brahmin, was purified by the horse sacrifice.
t.7.75.4: Long ago, it is said, O mighty-armed one, during the clash between the gods and the asuras, there was a great Daiteya named Vṛtra, esteemed throughout the worlds.
t.7.75.5: Spread out a hundred yojanas wide and rising three times as high, he looks upon the three worlds on every side with devotion and out of affection.
t.7.75.6: Knowing dharma and grateful, and firmly established in wisdom, he ruled the whole earth according to dharma, fully composed and attentive.
t.7.75.7: While he was ruling then, the earth yielded every desire like the wish-granting cow, and roots and fruits sprang forth full of rich flavour.
t.7.75.8: The earth of that great-souled one yields crops without being ploughed and is richly abundant; he enjoys a kingdom of such a kind, prosperous and wondrous to behold.
t.7.75.9: The thought arose in him: "Let me perform unsurpassed austerity, for austerity is indeed the highest good, and austerity is indeed the highest happiness."
t.7.75.10: Having established his eldest son as supreme lord over the citizens, he undertook fierce austerity, scorching all the deities.
t.7.75.11: While Vṛtra was practising austerities, Vāsava, as though in deep distress, approached Viṣṇu and spoke these words.
t.7.75.12: O mighty-armed one, through his austerities Vṛtra has conquered the worlds. For he is powerful and righteous of soul; I shall not be able to subdue him.
t.7.75.13: If he should undertake austerity yet further, O lord of the gods, then for as long as the worlds endure, so long will they remain subject to his will.
t.7.75.14: And you, O mighty one, are disregarding this supremely exalted being; for if you were angered, O lord of the gods, Vṛtra would not survive even a moment.
t.7.75.15: For ever since he came into a bond of affection with you, O Viṣṇu, from that time on he has obtained lordship over the worlds.
t.7.75.16: Therefore, O greatly renowned one, grant your grace to the worlds, for by your doing the whole world would become tranquil and free from decay.
t.7.75.17: O Viṣṇu, all these dwellers of heaven are looking to you; by the great slaying of Vṛtra, render them aid.
t.7.75.18: For you have always given help to these great-souled ones; this is beyond the power of others to bear. You are the refuge of those who have no refuge.
